To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Corin is present in human heart, kidney and blood, with the pro-BNP processing occurring in the circulation.
The expression levels of the genes encoding the natriuretic peptides and their receptors are altered in the heart, kidney, blood, and adipose tissue of obese mice.
the expression and processing of Corin are increased in the failing heart and that the increased expression of Corin is a consequence of pressure overload.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of drugs that can be used to control the progression of chronic heart failure.

the development of a new method of treatment of patients with severe heart failure, using a combination of the ACE inhibitor enalapril and the vasodilator nitrates, in order to reduce the high circulating levels of the vasoconstrictor peptide endothelin-1.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms of action of Corin and the development of novel Corin-based therapeutics for the treatment of heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a single biomarker, either BNP or NT-proBNP, for diagnosis and risk stratification in patients with heart failure is recommended.
the evidence is inconclusive.

the evidence for the use of the BNP assay in the evaluation of patients with suspected heart failure is strong, whereas the evidence for the utility of the BNP test in the evaluation of dyspnea in patients with chronic pulmonary disease or in patients presenting to the emergency room is less strong.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Corin gene encodes a transmembrane protein with serine protease activity, which is expressed in heart, kidney, lung, and blood.
the Corin protein is present in the circulation and that the circulating form is the result of pro-B-type naphthylamide natriuretic protein processing.
the expression of the natriuretic peptides in the human heart is more complicated than previously appreciated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of Corin in the kidney may have an impact on the regulation of blood pressure and renal function.
the expression of the gene encoding corin, the enzyme that processes the precursor to brain natriuretic peptides, is reduced in the heart of patients with HF.
the human heart is capable of producing and processing pro-B-type natiuretic peptide (proBNP) to BNP and NT-proBNP.
